summary.text: 你 means “you.” Its visible form combines 亻, treated as the person-category element in one proposed analysis, and 尔, the simplified form of 爾; 爾/尔 was also used for “you/your.” The competing formation analyses remain unresolved, and this history does not establish a sound role for 尔 in 你.

formation.text: One reported analysis is phonosemantic: 亻 supplies the person category and 尔 a sound cue. A competing, unverified proposal reads 人 and 尔 together as “person” and “you.” The formation remains disputed because the available historical accounts do not directly establish how 你 was formed.

components.text: In one reported phonosemantic analysis, 亻 represents a person and contributes the semantic category. A competing proposal treats 人 and 尔 together ideographically; the available evidence does not establish 亻’s historical role in 你.

The right-side 尔 is proposed as the phonetic element. It is the standardized simplified form of 爾, which was used for “you/your”; 尔 is also described as a shortened form of 爾. In Modern Mandarin, 尔 ěr and 你 nǐ differ, and this comparison alone does not establish an ancient sound relationship or 尔’s role in 你.

sound_limitation.text: The present-day Mandarin readings ěr and nǐ do not establish an ancient sound relationship or 尔’s phonetic role in 你. One supplied secondary account gives Old Chinese *njelʔ for 尔 and *nɯʔ for 你, but these are not an independently verified matched comparison here.

sound.text: In Modern Mandarin, 尔 is ěr and 你 is nǐ. This comparison alone does not demonstrate an ancient sound relationship or 尔’s role in 你.

history.text: The dictionaries report 你 glossed as “you” in 集韻 and cite its use in 隋書. The earliest surviving written example and the date of the quoted wording remain unresolved. A small-seal-style rendering of 你 is a modern font construction, not an ancient form.

The reported graphic account describes 尔 as taking the upper part of 爾. Separately, 尔/爾 was used for “you/your.” This history of 尔 neither establishes that it depicts an object nor explains its proposed sound function in 你.

uncertainties.text: The phonosemantic and ideographic analyses of 你 are both reported, but no supplied historical account directly establishes its construction. The proposed sound analysis should therefore be treated as plausible, not certain.

No inspected source establishes whether 尔 originally depicted an object or provides an independently recoverable pronunciation for any such object-name. This limits an object-based interpretation of 尔’s own history; it does not by itself resolve 尔’s proposed phonetic role in 你.

Bare 你 is recorded in plural examples from historical works, while ordinary modern plural usage is documented in 你们. The cited evidence does not establish the present-day frequency or productivity of bare-你 plural use, or a dated semantic link from singular ‘you’.

senses.gloss: second-person pronoun, ‘you’; also used with plural reference in cited contexts
senses.period: Current singular use; bare 你 also occurs with plural reference in cited historical examples, whose present-day frequency is unresolved
senses.text: 你 is a current second-person pronoun meaning ‘you.’ Historical examples also show bare 你 referring to groups, as in ‘you two’ and ‘you all’; this does not establish that 你 itself is a plural pronoun or how frequent that use is today. Ordinary modern plural usage is documented in 你们. The exact earliest surviving occurrence and the date of quoted passages’ wording remain unresolved.

senses.period: attested in cited historical examples; present-day status unresolved
senses.text: A character dictionary records bare 你 in plural examples such as 你兩個 (‘you two’) and 你眾人 (‘you all’). These cited examples are from historical works; their frequency or productivity in present-day speech is not established here. This is distinct from the ordinary modern plural construction 你们, formed from singular pronoun 你 with 们.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish when the dictionary-recorded bare-你 plural examples arose, whether that use remains current or productive, or a semantic development linking it to the singular pronoun. The ordinary modern plural construction 你们 is separately documented.

limitations.text: No verified historical image of 你 is available here: the proposed small-seal-style image is a modern font construction, and the available 尔 glyph images do not have verified reuse terms.
